title: Vector quantization sanity: INT8/FP16 calibration workflow and cosine-sim guard
creator: Ethan Miller
body:
Summary:
This ticket defines and implements a repeatable calibration and validation workflow for embedding model quantization profiles targeting INT8 and FP16 execution paths. The goal is a lightweight production guard that detects meaningful cosine-similarity regressions after quantization changes and flags them for automatic rollback or human review. This complements existing per-layer calibration runs by adding sampling, anchor selection, and an ops-safe alerting policy tailored for high-cardinality embedding workloads.

Background & motivation:
We have observed intermittent downstream similarity regressions when switching quantization profiles (especially between INT8 kernels and FP16 fallbacks) for embedding models used in semantic search. Current calibration runs produce numeric stats but lack an operational similarity gate that is tuned for application-level impact. This work provides: (1) a defined dataset sampling and anchor selection method, (2) a scoring and thresholding procedure based on cosine similarity distributions, (3) automated canary/rollout rules, and (4) an ops runbook and dashboard instrumentation for quick triage.

Acceptance criteria (must be strings in this ticket):
- A documented calibration pipeline that produces per-profile similarity histograms and a pass/fail verdict for INT8 and FP16 variants.
- Canary rollout configuration that uses the similarity gate to automatically stop/rollback if median cosine drops > 0.015 or P95 drops > 0.03 for the canary cohort.
- Dashboard widgets (latency, token cost, cosine distribution, anchors failing metric) added to Console release runtime-1.21.
- Playbook steps for sample re-run, additional calibration (per-layer recalibration), and fallback to FP16 when required.

Proposed workflow (high level):
1) Sample selection: stratified sampling across corpora + customer-provided anchors. Default sample size 10k vectors per model (configurable). Samples split into evaluation and holdout anchors (80/20).
2) Baseline embedding generation: produce float32 (FP32) reference vectors on the current gold model build (pre-quant). Store KV cache for deterministic runs.
3) Calibration run: run internal calibration to compute scale/zero-point per-channel (for INT8) and dynamic ranges for FP16 path; persist quant tables and representative input indices.
4) Quantized embedding generation: generate embeddings using quantized runtime (INT8 and FP16 kernels) for evaluation set.
5) Scoring: compute cosine similarities between quantized vectors and the FP32 baseline for each example. Produce distribution metrics: median, mean, std, P90, P95, fraction below thresholds.
6) Decision rules: pass if median >= baseline_median - 0.012 AND P95 >= baseline_p95 - 0.025 AND fraction_below_0.8 < 0.001. Canary-specific thresholds are 1.25x tighter.
7) Canary rollout: route 2% of production traffic to quantized profile for 24h. Continuously recompute rolling similarity metrics on sampled live requests. Immediate rollback if canary triggers fail.
8) Operational alerts: Pager/SLO signals when similarity drop correlates with production error or search quality regression.

Evaluation datasets and anchor strategy:
- Public: S-Bench small corpus (1.2M sentences) used for synthetic checks.
- Internal: per-customer anchor sets stored in S3 (encrypted); allow operators to opt-in customers to canary cohorts.
- Anchor selection heuristic: pick 30% of anchors with highest intra-corpus variance (most sensitive), 30% of stable frequent queries, 40% random. This mix improves early detection of semantic shifts introduced by quantization.

Quant metrics and telemetry:
- Cosine distribution time series (per-model, per-profile): median, P90, P95, fraction below 0.9 and 0.8.
- Embedding magnitude drift: mean L2 norm delta vs baseline.
- Nearest-neighbor rerank delta: for a heldout query set, measure change in top-5 overlap.
- Correlate token-level latency and cost delta for quantized profiles.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We avoid requiring FP32 inference in production; baseline FP32 runs occur in offline calibration jobs. Live canary uses quantized variant vs stored FP32 baseline vectors.
- INT8 tends to compress well but can create long-tail failures on rare token patterns; anchor strategy aims to expose those.
- FP16 serves as a softer fallback for low-latency SLOs where INT8 causes unacceptable quality regressions.
- Thresholds above are empirical starting points; we'll tune during first two cycles.

Links to artifacts and PRs:
- Design doc: https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/l/c/QUANT-PROFILES-Design (internal)
- Calibrator prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1893
- Dashboard proto: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/quant-sanity

Runbook excerpt (short):
- On alert: 1) Pause canary, 2) run calibration rerun with larger sample and per-layer stats, 3) compare per-layer error heatmap, 4) if regression localized to specific layers, attempt per-layer scale adjust and redeploy; else fallback to FP16 profile.

Next steps (short-term):
- Implement evaluation harness in runtime/ops (owner: Priya)
- Add dashboard metrics and alerting rules (owner: Analytics)

2026-03-11 — Priya Narayanan: Drafted sampling heuristics and suggested canary % (2%). Will prototype scoring job this week.

2026-03-12 — Rafael Gutierrez (review): Suggested tightening P95 rule for canary and adding nearest-neighbor overlap metric. Also requested explicit encryption note for customer anchors. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-12 — Priya Narayanan: Prototype job finished locally; median deltas look within target for FP16 but INT8 shows a 0.02 median drop on legal-corpus subset. Moving to experiment phase.
